_note: Why each phrase is likely (or not) to be said on the call. Authored judgement, not scraped. Key = '<COMPANY>|<phrase>'. `lean` is our own probability estimate, recorded BEFORE the call so mention_settle.py can measure calibration against it. Where our lean sits below the market bid, that is a PASS — the market is asking more than we think it's worth.

ABNB|World Cup.why: The 2026 World Cup is co-hosted across North America and lands squarely in Airbnb's booking window. Management has already been framing it as a demand catalyst; a Q2 call weeks out from the tournament almost certainly references it in guidance or the host-city narrative.

CELH|PepsiCo.why: PepsiCo is Celsius's distribution partner and a major shareholder. Distribution economics come up on essentially every Celsius call — it is hard to discuss shelf velocity or margin without naming the partner.

CELH|Vibe.why: Brand-language phrase rather than an operational one. Celsius does talk about brand energy, but 'Vibe' is a specific word that may not surface unless a product line or campaign carries the name. Below the 0.82 bid — PASS.

LYFT|Waymo.why: Autonomy is the dominant analyst question for rideshare, and Lyft has an active Waymo partnership narrative. Even if management avoids it in prepared remarks, the Q+A almost always forces the competitive-autonomy question, and the rules include Q+A.

LYFT|Revenue.why: Near-certain filler word on any earnings call. The market bid of 0.79 looks like it is underpricing an almost-automatic mention — this is the cleanest of the near-term set.

NBIS|Nvidia.why: Nebius is a GPU-cloud operator; its capacity, backlog and capex are denominated in Nvidia hardware. Discussing fleet buildout without naming the supplier would be unusual.

DKNG|Alberta.why: Alberta's regulated market opening is DraftKings' live expansion story in Canada. Likely named in the state/province rollout list, but it is one specific jurisdiction among several — management could speak generically about 'new markets' instead. Roughly fair at the 0.86 bid, so no edge — PASS.

DKNG|Expansion.why: Generic operational word that DraftKings uses constantly for new-state rollout. Far more likely than the specific jurisdiction names priced near it.

DKNG|Retention / Retain.why: Customer retention and hold rate are core DraftKings metrics; the word appears in most of their operational discussion. Modest edge over the 0.76 bid.

VST|Production Tax Credit / PTC.why: Vistra's nuclear economics run through the PTC floor price, and it is a recurring topic in their guidance discussion. Slight edge over the 0.75 bid, though it depends on whether policy comes up this quarter.

WEN|Project Fresh.why: Named internal initiative. Companies reliably repeat their own branded program names on calls — that is what the naming is for.

WEN|Inflation.why: Commodity and labour inflation is standard QSR margin commentary, and Wendy's has been discussing beef costs. Small edge over the 0.85 bid.

WEN|App.why: Digital ordering is Wendy's growth narrative; app/loyalty metrics appear in nearly every quarter's remarks.

HIMS|Peptide.why: Peptides are central to Hims's compounded-product and longevity roadmap, and management has leaned into the category. Roughly fair at the 0.81 bid — thin edge.

HIMS|Longevity.why: Longevity is an explicitly announced Hims vertical. Named strategic verticals get repeated on calls; the 0.77 bid gives a modest edge.

HIMS|Lab Testing.why: Lab testing underpins the personalisation and diagnostics push. Likely but not certain to be phrased exactly this way — management may say 'diagnostics' or 'biomarkers' instead, and the rule needs this phrase.

HIMS|FDA.why: Hims operates in compounded GLP-1s under active FDA scrutiny; regulatory status is the single most-asked analyst question. Q+A alone makes this near-certain. The 0.85 bid is the biggest gap to our lean in the near-term set.

HIMS|Canada.why: International expansion is real, but Canada specifically is one geography among several and may lose out to 'international' or the UK/Europe assets. Below the 0.75 bid — PASS.

CAVA|Salmon.why: Cava's grilled-salmon launch has been their headline menu-innovation item, and new LTO/menu items are standard call material. Edge over the 0.79 bid.

AAOI|Tariff.why: Applied Optoelectronics has China manufacturing exposure, so tariffs are plausible — but with only 36 open interest this is an illiquid market and the phrase may not surface if the quarter is quiet on trade policy. Below the 0.76 bid — PASS.
